acceptance.method: diagnostic (generate with-guide vs isolated baseline, LLM judge vs rubric acceptance)
guide_faults: The guide's 'one function = one responsibility, extract helpers' rule carries no judgment caveat against extracting a trivial one-line regex match into a separate function — that literal-minded extraction is what produced the with-guide output's actual defect: a confusingly near-duplicate name (`withoutSeparators` local var vs `withoutSeparors` function) with a typo, self-flagged but left unfixed in the delivered file.
acceptance.verdict: Both outputs already hit single quotes/braces/full-names/small-functions on their own; the guide's only clear, demonstrable win was forcing the @shared alias import, while its literal 'extract everything' pressure produced a self-admitted typo'd helper (and a `function` keyword the guide itself bans) that the cleaner, more feature-complete isolated baseline never had — net effect roughly a wash, tilted slightly negative.

checklist.note: Plain style-guide prose, no directives steering the reading agent's behavior beyond the stated coding rules.
No mention of sending any data anywhere; skill only edits/greps local files.
Only grep commands shown for self-check (grep -nE for quotes/relative imports); nothing destructive.
No base64/hex/eval or unreadable logic anywhere.
No scripts/ or references/ exist; SKILL.md contains no network calls or download instructions.
No reference to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, keychain, or cookies.
No sudo, setuid, or persistence mechanisms; skill directory contains only SKILL.md, no scripts/ or references/ subfolders.
